Question Text: Which velocity-vector description correctly represents 9 m/s south?
Answer 1: An arrow pointing south with a length/label representing 9 m/s
Answer 2: An unlabeled dot with no direction
Answer 3: An arrow pointing opposite south with any length
Answer 4: A number 9 with no direction

Question Text: Compare the two velocity vectors. Determine whether the object’s velocity changes from v₁ to v₂ and identify the evidence in the arrows.
Answer 1: The velocity changes because the vectors differ in magnitude, direction, or both.
Answer 2: Velocity cannot change unless the object stops.
Answer 3: Only arrow color matters.
Answer 4: The vectors always represent the same velocity.

Question Text: The dots mark equal time intervals. Describe the motion shown, connect the changing spacing to velocity, and critique the claim “equal time intervals always mean constant velocity.”
Answer 1: The object is slowing down; changing dot spacing means the velocity magnitude changes. Equal time intervals do not imply constant velocity.
Answer 2: The object must have constant velocity because times are equal.
Answer 3: Dot spacing shows mass, not motion.
Answer 4: The diagram gives no information about motion.
